reaction.episode: CORRECTION episode, data through November 13 and not stale: SPX is 3.61% below its 120-day high, 1.38% below its 50-day and 3.02% above its 200-day; SMH at $486.75 is inside Zone 2 after a 27.55% drawdown, NVDA at $162.85 is below its Zone 2 floor after a 33.09% drawdown; VIX 19.3 with no rollover, HY OAS 3.2 calm, and the mechanical capitulation tally is 2 of 4.
reaction.invalidation: The Probe stance is wrong if HY OAS breaks above 4% with SPX below its 200-day (credit-led rollover, not rotation), or if SMH falls through $470 and NVDA through $150 without any capitulation signal — either voids the ladder and forces a full re-audit of zones.

ladder.response: Re-arm Tranche A: staged probe buys in Zone 2 names (SMH complex, NVDA on reclaim of $175), sized small — preparation becomes action only on the third confirmation
ladder.trigger: Tally reaches 3 of 4 (volume climax reversal or VIX rolling over from the 19.92 five-day high) while SMH holds $470–505

ladder.response: Escalate down the ladder: hold probes, do not average down into the break — wait for the deeper zone and a fresh tally; no new capital until a lower zone prints and holds
ladder.trigger: SMH breaks below $470 (Zone 2 floor) or NVDA breaks below $150 with volume above its 196.6M 20-day average

ladder.response: Trap case: treat the bounce as a bull trap — do not chase, trim any probe bought in the bounce, and reset the ladder to the failure-zone verdict before re-entering
ladder.trigger: SMH or SPX bounces into the failure zone (SMH $580–600, SPX $7,750–7,820) and fails there on a closing basis

ladder.response: Stand down: rotation becomes rollover — stop all probing, move to Watch, and re-audit zones and ratios before any further deployment
ladder.trigger: HY OAS breaks above 4% or SPX closes below its 200-day at 7,340.32

ladder.response: Re-entry confirmed: the correction is resolving upward — promote Probe to Add on the names whose fundamentals already lead price (NVDA, AVGO, ONTO, DDOG)
ladder.trigger: SMH holds a close above $580–600 (failure zone) with the tally at 3 of 4 or better, or SPX reclaims $7,750–7,820

reaction.trapRisk: The live trap is a bounce into the SMH $580–600 / SPX $7,750–7,820 failure zone that fails: with the tally at only 2 of 4 and no VIX rollover, the first bounce is the most likely place to get caught. Entries wait for the failure-zone retest verdict — no chasing the first bounce, no sizing up on a one-day reclaim, and any probe bought in a bounce gets trimmed on failure at the zone.

strategyPosture: Probe, not Add: the tape is a CORRECTION with the AI complex inside buy zones (SMH Zone 2, NVDA below its Zone 2 floor) and credit calm, but the mechanical capitulation tally is only 2 of 4 — no volume climax, no VIX rollover — so entries stay small, staged, and zone-bound.

themes.counterRead: The divergence is real but not a buy signal by itself: NVDA's decline reason is ACUTE_CATALYST (the Huang resignation/FBI investigation overhang), not pure sentiment, and the mechanical tally is only 2 of 4 — no volume climax, no VIX rollover. The opportunity is in staged, zone-bound probing (NVDA is below its $175–185 Zone 2 floor; SMH at $486.75 is inside Zone 2), not in calling the bottom.
themes.dataAnchor: The hard data disagrees with a broken-business story: NVDA revenue is growing 61.4% YoY while the stock sits 33.1% below its 52-week high at $162.85 with RSI 24.9 (oversold). AVGO revenue is up 55% YoY with 67.8% gross margin and $26,914M free cash flow while 29.9% below its high. ONTO revenue is up 41.5% YoY, DDOG 27.7% YoY with 80% gross margin — all three flagged as the setup where fundamentals and price move in opposite directions. Of the 33 dislocations, most are classified SENTIMENT_DRIVEN, not fundamental.
themes.label: AI complex: price has fallen past the fundamentals
themes.narrative: The market narrative is that the AI trade is broken — NVDA down 25.88% in a month, SMH down 27.55% from its 120-day high, and the whole AI supply chain repriced as a bubble deflating.
themes.watchFor: NVDA reclaiming $175 (Zone 2 floor) on volume above its 20-day average of 196.6M shares, or the mechanical tally moving to 3 of 4.

themes.counterRead: Rotation is the base case, not a guarantee: the divergence itself is real and worth tracking, and credit conditions can flip — HY OAS at 3.2 is calm today, but it is the tripwire. If the unwind spreads from Mag7/AI into the broad index (SPX losing its 200-day at 7,340) the read flips from rotation to rollover.
themes.dataAnchor: The index tape does not confirm a rollover: SPX is only 3.61% below its 120-day high, 1.38% below its 50-day and still 3.02% above its 200-day. The concentration read is ROTATION_NOT_ROLLOVER — Mag7 averages 16.43% below 52-week highs versus SPY at 3.5%, a 12.93-point gap, while bank lending standards are LOOSE (SLOOS 1.7%, far below the ~40% stress threshold) and HY OAS is 3.2 and calm. AAPL, the strongest Mag7 name, is just 1.3% off its high.
themes.label: Rotation, not rollover: the index is holding while leadership unwinds
themes.narrative: Headlines read as a broad market break — QQQ down 2.02% on the day and 7.38% in a month, with December-hike talk replacing cut hopes.
themes.watchFor: SPX closing below its 200-day moving average of 7,340.32, or HY OAS breaking above 4%.

themes.counterRead: Multiple compression is the mechanism, and it cuts both ways: if the December FOMC validates the hawkish repricing, the compression continues into names still holding up; if the minutes or PCE (November 25) soften the path, the most compressed quality names re-rate first. The trade is not to fight the rate tape but to separate compression (reversible) from deterioration (NOW and ROK both flag DETERIORATING revenue inflection).
themes.dataAnchor: The curve prices exactly that: 10-year at 5.10%, 2-year at 4.86%, 30-year at 5.43%, 2s10s un-inverted at +0.24, real 10-year 2.86%. The damage shows up as MULTIPLE_COMPRESSION, not earnings collapse: AMAT is 49.9% below its high, KLAC 50.4%, TER 48.9%, ETN 26.2% — all flagged multiple compression while their businesses keep generating cash.
themes.label: Rates repricing is compressing multiples, not earnings
themes.narrative: The rate narrative has flipped from cuts to hikes — headlines say a larger-than-normal December hike now looks more likely and rate-cut hopes are fading, with FOMC minutes due November 18 and the decision December 8–9.
themes.watchFor: FOMC minutes November 18 and PCE October on November 25; a 10-year sustained move in either direction off 5.10% with HY OAS still at 3.2.

themes.counterRead: Insider buying and cheap P/S are supporting evidence, not a floor: VST's revenue inflection in the promotion screen reads STABLE_OR_DECLINING, and the whole theme trades as an AI proxy — if SMH keeps falling, power names fall with it regardless of their own books. Entry logic is the 50-day at $145.08 as the next leg, not the current price.
themes.dataAnchor: VST is a conviction promotion (score 83) at $133.01, 29.7% below its high: insiders bought $1.17M at the trough, revenue is growing 19.1% YoY, free cash flow is $1,318M, and P/S is 2.5x. The theme's decline reason is SENTIMENT_DRIVEN, and VST's Q3 print already confirmed guidance to the upside.

themes.narrative: The power theme got sold with everything AI-adjacent — VST down 15% in a month, SMR down 25.55%, OKLO down 22.56%, CCJ down 15.57%, GEV down 14.73%.

themes.counterRead: There is no divergence to exploit here, only risk to manage: the unwind is mechanical and the products will keep bleeding while the underlying chops. The question is not whether these bounce — it is whether the portfolio's sizing assumes a bounce that the structure cannot deliver in a sideways tape.

The underlying move is a normal correction (SPX only 3.61% off its high); the leverage is the amplifier, not the cause — daily-reset products decay in both directions.
